description: Shared conformance cases for rich text in database Text cells (spec: RICH_TEXT_FORMAT.md). Copies must stay byte-identical: AppFlowy-Web src/application/database-yjs/fields/text/__tests__/rich-text-conformance.json and AppFlowy-Premium frontend/resources/rich_text/rich_text_conformance.json (read by the Dart tests and the Rust tests). Dates have no time zone so they read the same in every zone. `pageNames` is what the page-name resolver knows.

envelope.description: a cell (stored field_type, data, raw rich_text; an absent key means the cell has none) under a field of type fieldType -> state plain|invalid|stale|rich|newer, whether this version may edit it, and the sanitized delta it shows (null: show data). Runners: web parse, Rust state/editable only (Rust does not sanitize), Dart rt64/editable helper.

cases.description: a cell without rich_text is plain
an empty rich_text (cleared by Desktop) is plain
a null rich_text reads like an absent one
an envelope without v (pre-versioning builds) reads as version 1
a version 1 envelope is rich and editable
min_v 1 is no requirement for version 1
an integer-valued min_v written as 1.0 is 1
a newer writer's additive formatting (no min_v) stays editable and keeps the unknown attribute
min_v above this version makes the cell read-only; known formatting still shows
a newer envelope whose delta this version cannot read is read-only and shows data
a min_v that is not a number is unknown: read-only
a fractional min_v is malformed: read-only
min_v 0 is malformed: read-only
a negative min_v is malformed: read-only
a boolean min_v is malformed: read-only
a null min_v reads like an absent one
a huge but finite integer-valued min_v is newer
a number outside the double range anywhere makes the value unparseable (as serde_json rejects it)
staleness is checked before min_v: a stale newer envelope is stale and editable
formatting saved for other text is stale
a value that is not JSON is invalid
a JSON value that is not an object is invalid
an envelope without text is invalid
an envelope whose text is not a string is invalid
a version 1 envelope whose delta is not a list is invalid
a version 1 delta with a non-string insert is invalid
attributes that are a list make a version 1 delta invalid
a delta that formats nothing (null attributes) is plain
attributes that are only false or null format nothing
a malformed v is informational and ignored
unknown top-level envelope keys are ignored
a rich_text that is not a string can only come from a newer representation: read-only
formatting in a cell written by another type is ignored
a Text-written newer cell under a field now typed URL shows plain but stays read-only
an escaped lone surrogate makes the value unparseable (serde_json rejects it)
with duplicate keys the last one wins in every parser
an empty object is invalid
a mention stored as JSON text reads as an object
a newer envelope with only unknown attributes is still read-only
a version 1 delta whose only attribute is unknown is formatted (kept)
with a duplicate min_v the last one wins in every parser, including Rust (no derived struct)
a number outside the double range inside the delta makes the whole value unparseable, even with min_v 2
an escaped lone surrogate inside the delta makes the whole value unparseable, even with min_v 2
an escaped lone surrogate in an object key makes the value unparseable
a cell without field_type is Text-written
a cell without field_type is Text-written whatever the field is now: a newer one stays read-only
a null field_type reads like an absent one
a field_type stored as the string "0" (older web) is Text-written
a field_type stored as the string "6" is not Text-written
a legacy source_field_type 0 makes the cell Text-written even if field_type says otherwise
field_type 0 is Text-written even with a legacy source_field_type of another type
an integer-valued float field_type 0.0 is 0
a field_type that is not an integer (here a boolean) reads like an absent one: Text-written

sanitize.description: a structurally valid delta -> the delta a version 1 client keeps and would write back unchanged: known attributes sanitized, unknown attributes preserved or dropped per the unknown-value rules, one output insert per input insert. There is no per-value size cap (RICH_TEXT_FORMAT.md R27.5 was removed on 2026-10-02); ids san-018 and san-026 belonged to it and are retired, not reused. Runners: web and Dart sanitizers; Rust does not sanitize.

cases.description: on/off marks are kept only as true
links and equations are kept only as non-empty strings
a known string mark has no length cap of its own (the delta limit bounds it)
colors are kept as hex, rgb(a) or theme tokens; anything else is dropped
a mention stored as JSON text is written back as an object
a mention without a non-empty type is dropped; other attributes stay
registered mention fields keep only their type; a numeric person_name becomes its digits
unknown mention fields are preserved by the unknown-value rules
a legacy reminder mention is written as a date mention
a mention's data object keeps title as a string and unknown members by the unknown-value rules
unknown attributes with valid keys and values are preserved
unknown attributes that are false or null are absent
unknown keys must be lower snake case, start with a letter and be at most 64 characters
prototype keys are never kept, at any depth
editor-internal and document-transient keys are reserved and never stored
unknown values nest at most 4 levels; a deeper value is dropped whole
integers beyond 2^53-1 are dropped (they cannot round-trip through JavaScript)
at most 32 unknown keys per attributes object are kept: the first 32 in UTF-16 code-unit order of their keys
unknown attributes on a mention or equation are preserved
arrays of valid values are preserved
attributes that end up empty are omitted
a mention of an unknown type is preserved with its label
a mention label that is not a string is dropped
the 32 kept keys are chosen by sorted key order, not by the order they appear in the input
an empty array or object has depth 1 and is preserved; depth is counted through empty containers
inside a mention, unknown fields and data members keep false; only null is dropped
an unknown value has no size cap of its own (only the 200,000-byte delta cap bounds it): large strings and arrays within the structural rules are kept
an integer-valued float is an integer for the safe-integer rule: 1.0 and -9007199254740991.0 are kept, 9007199254740992.0 and 1e21 are dropped
the 32-key cap (R27.6) applies only to attributes objects, mentions and mention data: an object nested inside a kept unknown value keeps all its keys

editability.description: an existing cell (or none), the field's current type, and a write -> result allowed (performed) | noop (nothing written, reported as success) | refused (nothing written, the update notice is shown) | skipped (a bulk operation proceeds for other cells and leaves this one untouched), and what happens to the formatting: kept | cleared | written | copied (the copy's rich_text is byte-identical and the copy is Text-written exactly when the original is). Write kinds: setText, setRichText, clearFormatting, clearCell (also clear field), duplicateRow, moveCard (board group move), setRelation, setDateRange (calendar/timeline drag), undoOwnEdit (database undo/redo restoring data), switchFieldType {from,to} (bulk materializers), normalizeLegacyFieldType (web legacy source_field_type normalizer). Runners: web (every guarded helper of RICH_TEXT_FORMAT.md section 13.3), Rust (update_cell, batch_update_cells, update_rich_text_cell, clear_cell, clear_field, duplicate_row, switch_to_field_type materializers).

notificationTitle.description: a row title (the primary field's plain text) -> the view_name a cell or title mention notification sends (MENTION_NOTIFICATIONS.md section 4): line breaks become spaces, the result is trimmed, and a title longer than notificationTitleMaxCodeUnits UTF-16 code units is cut to at most one less at an extended grapheme cluster boundary and ends with U+2026. null means: send the client's localized placeholder. Runners: web (Intl.Segmenter), Dart (package:characters).
